draft.title: The protein secretory pathway
card: Some proteins are made to leave the cell, such as the hormone insulin and digestive enzymes. They follow the secretory pathway.
These proteins are made by ribosomes on the rough endoplasmic reticulum (rough ER). They enter the ER and are folded there. The ER then packs them into vesicles, small sacs made of membrane.
The vesicles travel to the Golgi apparatus and fuse with it. The Golgi modifies the proteins, sorts them and packs them into new vesicles.
A vesicle moves to the cell surface membrane and fuses with it. The protein is released outside the cell. This is exocytosis.
draft.remember: Rough ER, vesicle, Golgi, vesicle, then exocytosis out of the cell.

a.q: In which order does a secreted protein pass through these structures?
opts: Rough ER, Golgi apparatus, cell surface membrane
Golgi apparatus, rough ER, cell surface membrane
Rough ER, cell surface membrane, Golgi apparatus
Cell surface membrane, Golgi apparatus, rough ER
a.why: The protein is made at the rough ER, then modified and sorted in the Golgi, then released at the cell surface membrane. Putting the Golgi first is tempting, but the protein is made on the rough ER.
a.clue: Start where the ribosomes make the protein.

b.q: Cells in a gland make a digestive enzyme for release outside the cell. A drug stops vesicles from fusing with the cell surface membrane. What happens to the enzyme?
opts: It builds up in vesicles inside the cell
It is made but released by the rough ER
It is no longer made on the rough ER
It is released through the Golgi apparatus
b.why: Exocytosis needs vesicles to fuse with the cell surface membrane. If they cannot, the enzyme stays inside the vesicles. Making the enzyme on the rough ER happens earlier, so it is not stopped.
b.clue: Which step happens at the cell surface membrane?

a.best: Rough ER, Golgi apparatus, cell surface membrane

b.best: It builds up in vesicles inside the cell
